chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you are in the seventh circuit, go to Al-Muta'awwaz, which is where you stand at the back of the Kaaba, parallel to the Door, and say: O Allah! The House is Your House, and the servant is Your servant, and this is the place of the one seeking refuge with You from the Fire. O Allah! From You is the comfort and the relief.' Then touch the Yamani corner, then go to the Stone and finish with it.

key_terms.الْمُتَعَوَّذ: Al-Muta'awwaz (the place of refuge, i.e., Al-Multazam)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and ritual action at Al-Multazam during the seventh circuit of Tawaf?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, Al-Multazam is revered as a place where supplications are accepted, and this hadith highlights the specific ritual of seeking refuge from Hellfire while standing between the Kaaba's door and the Yamani corner. The instruction to conclude the Tawaf by pressing one's chest and face against the Black Stone (Istikhram) emphasizes the physical manifestation of humility and connection with the Divine. This practice underscores the spiritual significance of the seventh circuit, often associated with the completion of the pilgrimage's core rites.
